You are in an **Archon Horizon** workspace at `.`.

Load the **`horizon`** skill FIRST. Read it at the ABSOLUTE path
`/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` (also exported as `$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`) — do NOT use a
relative path like `.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md`, which fails when your
shell starts in a member project rather than the workspace root. The skill
explains where the state lives, the tools, and this workspace's conventions
(one-shot discipline, git commits, the final report).

Before modifying files, inspect the required and conversational inbox lanes:
`"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json`
then `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json`.
Protections are standing constraints even when already read. Address or explicitly
acknowledge unread conversations before ordinary advisory inbox material.

# Task
Task: ajcr-charts
Title: C9 chartLocus, the chart pair, and DAT-B/DAT-C coverage
Project(s) — work across all of them:
- Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
References: roadmap=AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.c9b,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus.chart-u,AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b; inbox=I-0492,I-0494

BUILD THE CHART LAYER: chartLocus and the (f, hf) chart pair, then close DAT-B coverage/injectivity and DAT-C Sigma-charts. Roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus (with .c9b and .chart-u) plus dat-b and dat-c. C9 is the sole gate of DAT-B B-6 AND of the whole dat-glue assembly, so this is the second-highest-leverage lane in the project.

FOUR DELIVERABLES.

 (1) CHART-U(a)/(b) — THE CO-SIGNED BRICK, and start here because nothing in the tree implements it. chartLocus c lambda (w4-datc-worksheet.md section 3.3, CHART-U(a)) is a locus over a GENERAL TEST T indexed by a plus class lambda, and isOpen_chartLocus is CHART-U(b). Its node names three missing inputs — read them before writing. This is a genuine construction task, not a proof-hunting one, and it is developable PARAMETRICALLY, i.e. without waiting for the certificate lane.

 (2) C9a IS DONE, C9b IS THE DELIVERABLE PROPER. chartLocus is already DEFINED and OPEN at the parameter-space carrier level (the C9 split of 2026-07-26). What remains is f_c, the chart morphism, and the (f, hf) pair that pic0RepresentableByOfCharts (Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) consumes. HONEST GATE, corrected and adversarially verified: c9b is NOT merely divRep-gated — read its node for what the real gate is, and note it is developable parametrically ahead of CERT-Sigma.

 (3) DAT-B COVERAGE AND INJECTIVITY: every pic^0 point is Zariski-locally a chart point. Coverage-drop, separably-closed points, divisor-family field surjectivity, local chart openness and fibre-field invariance are ALL LANDED — what remains is B5/B6/chart-locus packaging, which is exactly what (1) and (2) unblock.

 (4) DAT-C SIGMA-CHARTS: C0-C5 are landed. C6-C8 and the canonical-section certificate depend on the certificate/divRep chain — take them as far as the frozen shapes allow and say plainly where you stopped.

ONE SCARE ALREADY CLOSED, do not re-open it: the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis at Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79 is REDUNDANT, not a gap — Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130/:140 supply it as instances and the module is in the import closure (record at Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210). That file also proves Smooth => GeometricallyReduced in mathlib generality and is flagged as an upstreaming candidate.

WORKSHEET-FIRST IS THE HOUSE RULE on this lane: w4-datc-worksheet.md governs, and where a node says WORKSHEET-FIRST the worksheet section is written or updated BEFORE the Lean.

CONCURRENCY IS BINDING. Four AJCR teams at once. Follow informal/protocol-concurrent-lanes.md exactly: private-index compare-and-swap ledger commits (never a bare git commit), and the mkdir lake mutex at /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock (DIRECTORY lock; never flock it).

COORDINATION. You consume the divRep endpoint from ajcr-divrep and the widened DivFamZar shape from ajcr-cert-r2 — but the point of this lane is that CHART-U and C9b are developable PARAMETRICALLY in those shapes, so do not idle waiting. State your assumed shape on the AJCR conversation thread and ask them to confirm or correct it. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild.

This is a headless, one-shot session: advance the REAL objective, commit each
verified unit and any final edits, keep operational comments to the delta,
then write the skill's brief final report.

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is

---
name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.

said it does "not silently assume the transport" because isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower
was "the honest statement" of when kappa(t)-level hfib gives the L-level hplus. THAT DECLARATION

docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked). Not a dangling reference: the sentence made hplus read as
bookkeeping already discharged, while hplus was the WHOLE of B-4's remaining content. The r6 row

along PicEtAff.map C L. Three functoriality laws -- PicEtAff.map_map, PicEtAff.map_unit, and

cechPicClass. All three had been in the tree for weeks; nobody composed them because the
docstring said somebody had. So the generalisation in L costs ZERO, which
isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self had already measured from below (Iff.rfl at L := kappa(t)) and the

the proof takes the A-structure from its htow argument and uses hplus at THAT instance only --

an Algebra A L unrelated to the composite A -> kappa(t) -> L the right-hand side pulls
D.cechPicClass along a DIFFERENT morphism and hfib cannot imply it. So the forall-form is not
merely hard to supply -- IT IS THE WRONG STATEMENT. Restated as

proof already destructures and then DISCARDS. This is price-the-instances-not-the-data occurring
INSIDE A BINDER -- quantifying one instance too freely turns a provable obligation into an
unprovable one, and a census cannot see it because the binder sits in an argument position.

WHAT LANDED (121390af6, 62dbd06c0):
 * Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean -- the transport; the tower-binder restatement;
   isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower, i.e. B-4's residue from hfib ALONE.

   W field consumes. A lane holding only IsOpen still has to bundle it, and that bundling step is
   where the haff cost got lost the first time.

leaf keeps producing is over-confident closure, three sessions running. The hypothesis is a
PER-AFFINE-PIECE EXISTENCE of a datum with the plus-class property, and NOTHING PRODUCES SUCH A

the datum's fibre class with mu's fibre, and for the Sigma-chart's specific mu it is where the

done, for exactly that reason.

I wrote that the endpoint is certificate-free "verified by the import closure". The IMPORT CLOSURE

purely incidentally. So a lane checking gatedness by grepping imports concludes the OPPOSITE of
the truth. What is true is the statement about the THEOREMS: walking transitive CONSTANT
dependencies gives 7445 / 7448 constants with ZERO matching Cert|DivFamZar|FinCover|Classify|
DivRep|divRep. Gatedness is cone-relative exactly like availability -- measure the declaration's
own closure, not the module's imports.

was false by exactly the one lemma proved at s0010. The IsIso hypothesis of the iso-invariance is
load-bearing, not packaging -- do not weaken it to an AlgHom.

98	Isolated as a definition because it is what the forward direction of
99	`IsChartDatumPresentation` actually consumes, and because it is a statement about the *naturality
100	of `cechPicClass` under base change to residue fields* — checkable independently of anything
101	about witnesses. -/
102	def IsChartDatumPlusFibre {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
103	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
104	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
105	    PicEtAff.map C (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
106	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
107	          (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ))
108	      = PicEtAff.unit C (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
109	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t))
110	            (Scheme.CechPic.map
111	              (relCurveMap C A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t))
112	              D.cechPicClass))
113	
114	/-! ## The forward half -/
115	
116	variable (C π) in
117	/-- **The forward half of `IsChartDatumPresentation`, pointwise.**
118	
119	If the datum presents `μ` at `κ(t)` as plus classes (`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, which mentions no
120	witness), then the datum's fibre predicate at `κ(t)` implies the split predicate for `μ`'s fibre.
121	
122	The proof is the **trivial splitting**: take `L := κ(t)`, the identity extension.  The witness
123	divisor the datum predicate hands over already lies in the right class and already has vanishing
124	`H¹`, so nothing has to be transported.  `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self` is the
125	instance of the introduction rule this needs, and it is the instance memory I-0564 recorded as
126	unelaborable — see its docstring in `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` for why staging the
127	existentials makes it a one-liner.
128	
129	Note what this does *not* need: no separability argument, no common refinement, no descent.  All
130	of that belongs to the converse. -/
131	theorem isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
132	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
133	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left)
134	    (h : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) :
135	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ) := by
136	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
137	  exact isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self C _ _ (hfib t) W hW hW1
138	
139	/-! ## The `↔`, with the owed direction named -/
140	
141	variable (C π) in
142	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` assembled** — the forward half proved, the converse named.
143	
144	Stated so that a lane closing CHART-U(b) sees exactly one obligation rather than two: given the
145	witness-free plus-class identity, the `→` direction is free, and what remains is `hconv`.
146	
147	`hconv` is the descent direction: from a split witness over *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)` chosen
148	per point, produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself.  Its two ingredients both exist —
149	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries a *datum* predicate across a field
150	extension, and `hfib` identifies the classes — but composing them is not a rewrite, because the
151	witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s at `κ(t)`.
152	
153	**`hconv` IS DISCHARGED as of 2026-07-29** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`,
154	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at`), and the diagnosis above was right about the
155	obstruction while **naming only two of the three ingredients**.  The step that makes the
156	received witness *visibly* lie in `D`'s class is not a transport at all: it is
157	`PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1), the unconditional
158	close of the ζ3 campaign) followed by `relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton`, which together force
159	the presenting class `M` to *equal* `D`'s fibre class at `L_t`.  Then
160	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` descends it, exactly as predicted.
161	
162	What the discharge consumes in place of `hconv` is the same plus-class identity as `hfib` but at
163	an arbitrary extension of `κ(t)` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt`); at `L := κ(t)` it *is* `hfib` by
164	`Iff.rfl`.  So use `isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` rather than supplying `hconv` by
165	hand — this theorem remains correct and is the general form. -/
166	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
167	    [Algebra k A] {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
168	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D)
169	    (hconv : ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
170	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ) →
171	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) :
172	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D :=
173	  fun t => ⟨isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing C π hfib t, hconv t⟩
174	
175	end

def picEtSubgroup :
    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def picEt : Type u :=
  picEtSubgroup C T

noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))

namespace picEt

variable {C T}

/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
  s.2 U V h

@[ext]
lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
  Subtype.ext (funext h)

variable (C T) in
/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype

@[simp]
lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (AlgHom.id k A) x := by
        rw [show Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) (le_top :
              (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens) ≤ (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens))
            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from Over.resAlgHom_rfl _ le_top,
          AlgHom.id_comp,
          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom
            = AlgHom.id k A from
            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).apply_symm_apply a]

/-- **The affine comparison isomorphism**: on an affine test `overSpec k A`, the
affine-opens limit `picEt` collapses by evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the
affine-opens poset to the one-step plus `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra. -/
def picEtAffineEquiv : picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A :=
  MonoidHom.toMulEquiv (picEtToAff C A) (picEtOfAff C A)
    (picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff C A) (picEtToAff_comp_picEtOfAff C A)

lemma picEtAffineEquiv_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtAffineEquiv C A s
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom

  rfl

lemma picEtAffineEquiv_symm_apply_val (x : PicEtAff C A)
    (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :

/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
étale-separated — proved separately). -/
def PicEtAff : Type u :=
  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))

namespace PicEtAff

/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
    ∀ q, motive q := by
  intro q
  induction q using Quotient.ind with
  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2

theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
    {y : descentClasses C F} :
    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
  Quotient.eq

/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
@[simp]
theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩

/-! ### The group structure -/

/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
    (x : descentClasses C E) :
    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
      = descentMap C f x := by
  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]

/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
    (y : descentClasses C F) :
    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
      = descentMap C g y := by
  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]

/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range

lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T

noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)

/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)

lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)

/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
    motive x :=
  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}

/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩

  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)

8	/-!
9	# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base
10	
11	This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
12	base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.
13	
14	## The obligation, and why it looked hard
15	
16	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
17	whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
18	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
19	class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
20	`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.
21	
22	The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
23	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
24	engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
25	false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
26	`Spec A`.
27	
28	## Why it is in fact free
29	
30	There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
31	field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
32	where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
33	map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
34	`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
35	hypothesis anywhere.
36	
37	Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
38	transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
39	`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
40	only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
41	which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
42	step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
43	the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.
44	
45	## What this does and does not give
46	
47	It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
48	(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
49	honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
50	to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
51	topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
52	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).
53	
54	So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
55	`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
56	lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
57	construction.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
62	  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
65	  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
66	-/

95	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **A plus class becomes the plus-unit of an honest class over its own cover carrier**, over
98	an ARBITRARY affine base `A` — no field, no finiteness, no separability.
99	
100	`PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x`: the class
101	presented by `x` on the cover `E` restricts, along `A → E.Carrier`, to the tautological plus
102	unit of `x` itself.
103	
104	This is the general-base analogue of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom`
105	(`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`) at `ℓ := AlgHom.id`.  That lemma carries `[Field K]`,
106	`[Field L]` because *its* consumer (the degree seam) reads a degree; the argument itself uses
107	neither.  The substantive content, identical in both, is the **descent condition** `x.2`: the
108	two ways of carrying `x` into the base-changed carrier — along `E.baseChangeInclude` and along
109	`Algebra.ofId` — agree on a descent class, which is what `relPicAlgMap_congr` consumes.

111	Why this matters: the tree's only previous route from a plus class to an honest one was étale
112	field-cofinality (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`), which is field-only, so "honesty over a general
113	affine base" was recorded as an unlanded *construction*.  It is not a construction at all — a
114	cover splits over its own carrier, and the identity map is the splitting. -/
115	theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
116	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
117	    PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
118	      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
119	  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)]
120	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)) (Subtype.ext ?_)
121	  rw [descentBaseChange_coe]
122	  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier)
123	    ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier (E.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier).restrictScalars A) x.2
124	
125	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
126	variable (C) in
127	/-- **Every plus class over an affine base is honest over some affine base above it** — the
128	existential form of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self`, which is how a consumer meets it: it does
129	not get to choose `B`, it gets a `B` from the class's own presentation.
130	
131	Compare `exists_splitting_of_picEt` (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`): that gives a *field*
132	extension and requires the base to be a field; this gives an étale extension and requires
133	nothing.  The two are the field and general-base halves of the same move, and the chart layer
134	needs both — the field one to read the split witness predicate at a point, this one to run the
135	engine over a base. -/
136	theorem exists_honest_of_picEtAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
137	    (a : PicEtAff C A) :
138	    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra k B) (_ : Algebra A B)
139	        (_ : IsScalarTower k A B) (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)),
140	      PicEtAff.map C B a = PicEtAff.unit C B z := by
141	  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
142	  | mk E x =>
143	    refine ⟨E.Carrier, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
144	      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)), ?_⟩
145	    exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x
146	
147	/-! ## The payoff: the engine's input, with honesty discharged -/
148	
149	variable (C π) in
150	/-- **The engine input, assembled**: for any plus class over any affine base `A` and any chart
151	index `(m, Z)`, once the class is read honestly over a base `B` above `A` by a Čech class `c`,
152	a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `B` presenting `c` twisted by the chart index exists.
153	
154	This composes the two halves that were previously recorded as separate gates:
155	
156	* honesty over `B := E.Carrier` — `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` above, which needs no field;
157	* presentation of the twisted class by a datum — `exists_cechPicClass_eq`, applied at the
158	  *product* class, which is why no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul` is needed
159	  (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`).
160	
161	The conclusion is exactly the input of
162	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`, so the openness of the witness
163	locus over `Spec B` is available for every plus class and every chart index.  What is *not* here
164	is the identification of that locus with `chartLocus` — that is `IsChartDatumPresentation`, the
165	one genuine remaining obligation of CHART-U(b).
166	
167	Stated with `c` as a hypothesis rather than bundled into the existential: bundling it forces the
168	elaborator to unify the tower instances on `B` while `B` is still a metavariable, which is the
169	hazard recorded at `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note.  A consumer obtains `B` and `c`
170	from `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` plus `relPicMk_surjective`, then applies this. -/
171	theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
172	    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (m : ℕ)
173	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
174	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
175	      D.cechPicClass
176	        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
177	  exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass c m Z
178	
179	end

155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of

158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the

163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
164	
165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.

167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and

185	
186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.

194	
195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in

199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
200	
201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
213	    apply Spec.map_injective
214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
216	  rw [h]
217	  rfl
218	
219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
221	
222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
226	particular along an isomorphism.
227	
228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
229	
230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
259	                    D.cechPicClass
260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
274	  rw [hset]
275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
276	
277	/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/
278	
279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
280	
281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
287	
288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
299	  (hpres t).symm
300	
301	/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/
302	
303	variable (C π) in
304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
305	over an affine test).
306	
307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
312	
313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
320	the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
329	  -- other pointwise.
330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
335	  rw [hset]
336	  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D
337	
338	end

9	/-!
10	# `hplus` from `hfib`: the tower transport CHART-U(b) was still owed
11	
12	## What this file closes, and why it was not already closed
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean` reduces CHART-U(b)'s residue
15	`IsChartDatumPresentation` to `hfib` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, the plus-class identity at each
16	residue field `κ(t)`) **plus** `hplus` — the same identity read at an arbitrary extension
17	`L/κ(t)` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt`).  Its own docstring names the missing link:
18	
19	> It does **not** silently assume the transport: `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` is
20	> the honest statement of when the `κ(t)`-level `hfib` gives the `L_t`-level one, and its
21	> hypothesis is a tower compatibility that the split witness's own instances supply.
22	
23	**`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` does not exist.**  It is named in that paragraph and
24	nowhere else in the tree — a declaration advertised by a docstring and never written, the failure
25	mode memory `docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked` records.  The consequence was not cosmetic:
26	the sentence made `hplus` look like bookkeeping already discharged, while `hplus` was in fact the
27	*whole* of B-4's remaining content.  That reading is what this file removes, by proving the
28	transport rather than citing it.
29	
30	## The mathematics, and why it is a transport and not a base-change theorem
31	
32	`hplus` at `L` asks for
33	
34	  `PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C κ(t) μ_t) = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C L (D_L))`
35	
36	where `D_L` is `D.cechPicClass` pulled to `L`, and `hfib` at `t` gives exactly that identity with
37	`L` replaced by `κ(t)`.  So apply the restriction homomorphism `PicEtAff.map C L` to `hfib t` and
38	identify both sides:
39	
40	* **Left.** `PicEtAff.map_map` over the tower `κ(t) → L`: restricting twice is restricting once,
41	  so `map C L (map C κ(t) x) = map C L x`.  The `κ(t)`-level `map` in `hfib` is `map C κ(t)`
42	  applied to the fibre, which `map_id` collapses — this is where the two spellings meet.
43	* **Right.** `PicEtAff.map_unit`, the naturality of the plus unit: the image of a unit is the unit
44	  of the transported `relPic` class.  Then `relPicAlgMap_mk` turns `relPicMap` of a `relPicMk`
45	  into `relPicMk` of a `CechPic.map`, and `relCurveMap_comp` — the *composition* law of the
46	  relative-curve comparisons over `k → A → κ(t) → L`, already landed in `DivisorFamilyMapAlg` for
47	  the divisor functor laws — identifies the two-step pull `A → κ(t) → L` with the one-step pull
48	  `A → L` that `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` names.
49	
50	So the transport is three functoriality laws and no geometry.  All three were in the tree; what
51	was missing is that nobody had put them together, because the docstring said somebody had.
52	
53	## The tower hypothesis is real, and it is `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L`
54	
55	The one thing the transport genuinely needs beyond instances already in scope is that the
56	`A`-algebra structure on `L` agrees with the composite `A → κ(t) → L`.  It is not automatic:
57	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` takes `[Algebra A L]` as a *separate* instance from
58	`[Algebra κ(t) L]`, so a caller could in principle supply an unrelated one, and then the
59	right-hand sides genuinely differ (the `CechPic` class pulled along `A → L` is not the one
60	pulled along `A → κ(t) → L`).  Naming it as a hypothesis is therefore the honest statement, and
61	it is exactly the third component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already produces — so the
62	composite below needs nothing from the caller that the descent step did not already have.
63	
64	## Main declarations
65	
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` — **the transport**, under the
67	  tower compatibility: `hfib` at `κ(t)` gives `hplus` at any `L`.  The declaration the converse
68	  file's docstring advertised.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower` — **CHART-U(b)'s residue from
70	  `hfib` ALONE**, with no `hplus` side condition: the transport supplies it at every point and
71	  every extension, and `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower.
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
77	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
78	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
79	
80	universe u
81	
82	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
83	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
84	
85	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
86	
87	open AlgebraicJacobian
88	
89	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
90	
91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
94	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
95	
96	noncomputable section
97	
98	/-! ## The transport -/
99	
100	variable (C π) in
101	/-- **THE TRANSPORT** — `hplus` at an arbitrary extension `L` from `hfib` at `κ(t)`.
102	
103	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartPresentationConverse`'s header advertises by name and which did
104	not exist.  Under the tower compatibility `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` — the one thing that is *not*
105	automatic, and the third component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns — the plus-class
106	identity at `κ(t)` implies the same identity at `L`.
107	
108	Proof: apply `PicEtAff.map C L` to `hfib t`.  `PicEtAff.map_map` collapses the two-step
109	restriction on the left; `PicEtAff.map_unit` moves it through the unit on the right; and
110	`relCurveMap_comp` over `A → κ(t) → L` identifies the two-step pull of `D.cechPicClass` with the
111	one-step pull `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` names.  Three functoriality laws, no geometry. -/
112	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
113	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
114	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
115	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
116	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] [Algebra A L]
117	    [IsScalarTower k A L]
118	    [IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
119	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
120	    IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L := by
121	  have h := congrArg (PicEtAff.map C L) (hfib t)
122	  rw [PicEtAff.map_map, PicEtAff.map_unit, relPicAlgMap_mk] at h
123	  refine h.trans (congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C L) (congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)) ?_))
124	  -- the two-step pull `A → κ(t) → L` is the one-step pull `A → L`.  Rewriting the RHS's
125	  -- morphism into the composite keeps the `CechPic` type index fixed, which is what makes
126	  -- this a legal `rw` where rewriting the LHS is not (the two spellings `relCurve C κ(t)`
127	  -- and `(C ⊗ overSpec k κ(t)).left` are `rfl`-equal but block the motive).
128	  rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := A)
129	      (R' := Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) (R'' := L),
130	    Scheme.CechPic.map_comp]
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-! ## The descent step with the tower restricted
134	
135	The transport above cannot be fed to `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` as it stands,
136	and the reason is a genuine finding about that theorem's statement rather than a typing nuisance.
137	Its `hplus` binder reads
138	
139	  `∀ (L) … (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L), IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L`
140	
141	— universally quantified over the `A`-algebra structure on `L`, with only the `k`-tower imposed.
142	That is **strictly stronger than the theorem consumes**: its proof obtains the `A`-structure from
143	its own `htow` argument and uses `hplus` at *that* instance only.  And the extra strength is not
144	harmless, because `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, which depends on the
145	`A`-algebra structure: for an `Algebra A L` unrelated to the composite `A → κ(t) → L`, the
146	right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a different morphism and the identity has no reason
147	to hold.  So the `∀`-form is not merely unprovable from `hfib` — it is the wrong statement, and
148	`hfib` cannot imply it.
149	
150	This is the failure mode `price-the-instances-not-the-data` names, occurring inside a binder: the
151	hypothesis quantifies instances, and quantifying one instance too freely turns a provable
152	obligation into an unprovable one.  So the step is restated below with the tower compatibility
153	`IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` in the binder — exactly the third component
154	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns and which the landed step already destructures and
155	then discards.  The proof is the landed one; only the binder changes. -/
156	
157	variable (C π) in
158	/-- **The descent step, with the `A`-tower in `hplus`'s binder** — otherwise
159	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` verbatim.
160	
161	The landed form asks for the plus-class identity at *every* `A`-algebra structure on `L`; this
162	asks for it only at those compatible with `A → κ(t) → L`, which is all its proof ever uses and
163	all that `hfib` can give (see the section note above).  With this binder the transport
164	`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` applies, and CHART-U(b)'s residue follows from `hfib`
165	alone. -/
166	theorem hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
167	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
168	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)
169	    (hplus : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
170	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
171	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
172	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
175	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
176	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
177	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
178	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := towerOfResidueFieldExtension (k := k) t L
179	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
180	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
181	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
182	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
183	    rw [← hM]
184	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow hATow
185	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
186	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
187	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
188	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
189	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
190	  rw [hW, hMcl]
191	
192	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue from `hfib` alone -/
193	
194	variable (C π) in
195	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` FROM `hfib` ALONE** — no `hplus` side condition.
196	
197	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` asks for `hfib` *and* the per-point identity at every
198	extension.  The transport above supplies the second from the first, and
199	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower instance the transport needs, so the caller
200	owes only `hfib`.
201	
202	**What this settles about the CHART-U(b) row.**  The row's state as of 2026-07-29 was "both
203	halves of the pointwise presentation are witness-free, and what remains is a `cechPicClass`
204	base-change identity at every extension of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`
205	asks".  That gap is now closed in the *cheap* direction the row did not expect: the extra
206	strength is not extra content, because the identity at `L` is the identity at `κ(t)` pushed
207	along `PicEtAff.map`.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measured the gap from below (at
208	`L := κ(t)` the two coincide by `Iff.rfl`); this measures it from above, and the two together say
209	the generalisation in `L` costs nothing.
210	
211	So `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's named residue, CHART-U(b)'s one remaining obligation, and
212	the thing `ChartLocusAffineLocal` reduces `haff` to — now rests on exactly one hypothesis:
213	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, a witness-free, `H¹`-free, divisor-free identity of plus classes at the
214	residue fields. -/
215	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
216	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
217	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
218	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D := by
219	  refine isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse C π hfib fun t hsplit => ?_
220	  refine hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower C π μ D t
221	    (fun L _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => ?_) hsplit
222	  exact isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower C π μ D t L hfib
223	
224	end

129	def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=

138	iso-invariance.

147	theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
148	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
149	    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :

151	        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
152	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
153	          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
154	  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
155	    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu
