160	/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**
161	
162	For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is
163	the preimage, along the carrier map of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, of `chartLocus` over `T`.
164	
165	Both sides unfold to the same split-witness condition read at two residue fields, so this is
166	`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
167	twist commutes with restriction). -/
168	theorem chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
169	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
170	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (lam : picEt C T) :
171	    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
172	      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam := by
173	  refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
174	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, mem_chartLocus_iff, mem_chartLocus_iff,
175	    ← picEtMap_chartTwist]
176	  exact isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff C hinv T U (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring
180	promises follows from the affine case "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s
181	transport (iii)".
182	
183	If `chartLocus` is open over every affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T`.
184	
185	The bookkeeping is genuinely bookkeeping — but note *which* bookkeeping, because it is not the
186	`isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter` the docstring names: the piece's locus lives in a **different
187	space** (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`), so the bridge is that the carrier map is an open
188	immersion whose range is `U` (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`).  The preimage identity
189	`chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage` then turns per-piece openness into openness of
190	`chartLocus ∩ U`, and the affine opens cover `T.left`. -/
191	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
192	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
193	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
194	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
195	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
196	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) := by
197	  -- Openness is local: it suffices that every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood
198	  -- inside it, and each point lies in some affine open of `T.left`.
199	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
200	  intro t ht
201	  -- an affine open around `t`
202	  obtain ⟨U, hUmem⟩ : ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens, t ∈ U.1 := by
203	    obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
204	      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
205	        (show t ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
206	    exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, hmem⟩
207	  -- the piece's locus is open, and its image is `chartLocus ∩ U`
208	  have hpre := chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C hinv m Z T U lam
209	  refine ⟨chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1, Set.inter_subset_left, ?_, ht, hUmem⟩
210	  -- `chartLocus ∩ U` is the image of the piece's locus under an open immersion with range `U`
211	  have hoi : IsOpenImmersion (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
212	  have hrange : Set.range (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base = (U.1 : Set T.left) := by
213	    change Set.range (U.2.fromSpec).base = _
214	    exact U.2.range_fromSpec
215	  have himg : (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ''
216	        (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
217	      = chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1 := by
218	    rw [hpre, Set.image_preimage_eq_inter_range, hrange]
219	  rw [← himg]
220	  haveI := hoi
221	  exact (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ (haff U)
222

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff
10	
11	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
12	charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the
13	instance
14	
15	```
16	[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
17	```
18	
19	which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
20	(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
21	`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
22	the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.
23	
24	## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here
25	
26	Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
27	every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
28	`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.
29	
30	For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
31	proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
32	B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
33	mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
34	`Sigma.desc`.
35	
36	The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
37	by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
38	`ChartsCoverLocally` below.
39	
40	## The honest scope, stated up front
41	
42	`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
43	is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
44	this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
45	producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
46	none to check.
47	
48	## Main declarations
49	
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
51	  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
52	  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
54	  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
56	  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
57	  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
58	-/
59	
60	set_option autoImplicit false
61	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

63	universe u

65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
66	
67	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
71	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
72	
73	noncomputable section
74	
75	variable (C) in
76	/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**
77	
78	For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
79	becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.
80	
81	This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
82	one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
83	producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
84	index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
85	that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
86	def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
87	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
88	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
89	    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T
90	
91	/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
92	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
93	
94	The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
95	the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
96	of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
97	covering sieve is covering.
98	
99	Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
100	imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
101	makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
102	exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
103	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
104	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
105	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
106	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
107	  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
108	    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
109	    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
110	    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
111	    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
112	    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
113	    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]
114	
115	/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**
116	
117	If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
118	holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
119	the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
120	the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
121	"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.
122	
123	Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
124	datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
125	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
126	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
127	    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
128	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
129	  intro T s
130	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_
131	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.top_mem T)
132	  intro T' g _
133	  exact le_iSup (fun j => Presheaf.imageSieve (f j) s) i g (hi (op T') _)
134	
135	end
136	
137	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: `IsChartUniv` reduced to one clause about the chart locus
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` splits `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` into the two
13	clauses mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative` actually conjoins, and gives a criterion whose
14	input is elementwise.  This file instantiates that criterion at the Abel chart and at
15	`V := chartLocus`, which is the pair `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
16	
17	The point is to make the residue **one named clause about the chart locus** instead of the
18	whole certificate.  Concretely, the criterion's `ChartFibrePresented` datum has four fields,
19	and at the Abel chart three of them are supplied here:
20	
21	| field | at the Abel chart | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `W` | `chartLocus` of the test point's class, as an open | **shape supplied here**, but at the
24	  cost of `haff` — see the retraction below |
25	| `r` | the divisor family over the locus | the classifier `divRepClassifyZar` |
26	| `sq` | its class is the test's class | the classifier's own characterisation |
27	| `exists_factor` | uniqueness of the normalized representative | **the relative form of GAP-2** |
28	
29	So `W` needs only B-4 (**not** "nothing" — retracted below), `sq` is a property of whatever
30	`r` is, and the genuine content is
31	concentrated in `r` (a construction, from the classifier) and `exists_factor` (relative
32	GAP-2).  This file makes that split machine-checkable: `IsChartLocusFibre` below names
33	exactly the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple **at the chart locus**, and
34	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` proves `IsChartUniv` from it.
35	
36	## Why this is not a restatement
37	
38	A reduction that merely renames its obligation is worthless, and this one is checked against
39	that failure mode in two directions:
40	
41	* `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised, so the `W` field is a *shape* a lane
42	  no longer has to invent.
43	
44	  **RETRACTED 2026-07-29, second clause only** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  This
45	  read "the `W` field costs zero, which is a real reduction of the datum from four fields to
46	  three".  The cost is not zero: `chartLocusOpens` takes the argument `haff`, and **nothing in
47	  the tree discharges it**.  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` removed the
48	  `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis but passes `haff` straight through, as does
49	  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it; the affine case that would feed it
50	  (`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`) is itself conditional on
51	  `IsChartDatumPresentation`, which is dat-b row B-4's named residue and is only half landed.
52	  So the datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  The
53	  residue is now named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4's own obligation by
54	  `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`;
55	* `isChartLocusFibre_of_isChartUniv` is the **converse**: `IsChartUniv` at the chart locus
56	  gives injectivity on every test, so a lane cannot obtain `IsChartUniv` while avoiding the
57	  content of `exists_factor`.  The reduction is therefore an equivalence in the direction
58	  that matters, not a weakening.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens` — `chartLocus` as an honest `T.Opens`, using the
63	  unconditional general-test openness.  This is the `V` that `restrictChart` wants.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartLocusFibre` — the residue: the `r`/`sq`/`exists_factor` triple
65	  of the criterion, at the chart locus, for every test point.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` — **the reduction**: that triple
67	  gives `IsChartUniv` (hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)` pair) at any open.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isChartUniv` — the converse-direction check.
69	-/
70	
71	set_option autoImplicit false
72	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
73	
74	universe u
75	
76	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
77	
78	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
79	
80	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
82	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
83	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
84	
85	noncomputable section
86	
87	/-! ## The chart locus as an open of the test
88	
89	`chartLocus` is a `Set T.left` and `restrictChart` wants a `T.Opens`.  The bridge is the
90	openness theorem.  **"which is now unconditional — so this costs a hypothesis-free definition
91	rather than a gate" is RETRACTED** (2026-07-29): the general-test openness theorem is
92	unconditional in `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` but still takes the affine-local `haff`, which
93	nothing discharges.  See `chartLocusOpens`' docstring and
94	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`. -/
95	
96	variable (C) in
97	/-- **`chartLocus` as an open subscheme of the test.**
98	
99	For a test `T` presented as `Over.mk a` and a class `lam` on it, the chart locus is open by
100	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditional since
101	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged), so it is an honest element of `T.Opens`.
102	
103	**THE `haff` SENTENCE HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED** (2026-07-29,
104	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageAbel.lean`).  It read: "The `haff` hypothesis is the affine-local
105	input of that theorem and is *not* a residue of this file: it is what the landed affine
106	openness supplies."  The landed affine openness does **not** supply it.
107	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`) is conditional
108	on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — dat-b row B-4's own named residue, whose *witness* half is now
109	discharged too (`hconv`, by plus-unit injectivity,
110	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`), leaving a plus-class base-change
111	identity — and no theorem in the tree produces `haff` for a general test.  It is a genuine
112	open obligation, named `ChartLocusAffineLocal` and reduced to B-4 by
113	`chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation`.  It is
114	carried as an argument here so the definition does not silently depend on a chosen route. -/
115	def chartLocusOpens (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
116	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
117	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
118	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
119	    T.left.Opens where
120	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
121	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal' C m Z T lam haff
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T}
126	    {haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
127	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))}
128	    {t : T.left} :
129	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
130	  Iff.rfl
131	
132	/-! ## The residue, named -/
133	
134	variable (C π n) in
135	/-- **The residue of C9b, named**: for every test point of the Σ-sheaf, the chart point over
136	its chart locus together with the two properties the criterion needs.
137	
138	This is `ChartFibrePresented` with its `W` field already discharged — it is `chartLocus`,
139	open unconditionally — so what a lane owes is precisely:
140	
141	* `r`: the divisor family over the locus whose class is the given one.  This is the
142	  classifier `divRepClassifyZar` applied to the canonical-section family, i.e. CHART-U(c)'s
143	  construction;
144	* `sq`: that its chart value *is* the given class, which is the classifier's characterising
145	  property;
146	* `exists_factor`: that two points with the same class agree, i.e. the **relative form of
147	  DAT-C GAP-2** (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` in families).
148	
149	Stated as a `Prop` over an arbitrary presenting datum rather than as a structure carrying the
150	family, because the family is the classifier's output and this lane must not guess its shape:
151	the existential is over morphisms of schemes only. -/
152	def IsChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
153	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
154	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
155	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) : Prop :=
156	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
157	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) g)
158	
159	/-- **THE REDUCTION**: the residue above gives `IsChartUniv`, hence the `hf` of the `(f, hf)`
160	pair, at *any* open of the divisor scheme.
161	
162	Two things are worth reading off the proof.  First, it goes through the criterion of
163	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` and then through the *composition* half
164	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` already landed in `Pic0ChartPair.lean` — so the two
165	halves of C9b compose exactly as the file headers predicted, with no seam.  Second, the open
166	`V` is arbitrary: restriction never has to be to the chart locus for `hf` to hold, because
167	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is stable under precomposition with an open immersion.  The chart
168	locus is where the *unrestricted* statement becomes true, which is a statement about
169	`IsChartLocusFibre`, not about `V`. -/
170	theorem isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
171	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
172	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
173	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
174	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
175	    (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg) (V : D.left.Opens) :
176	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
177	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V
178	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some)
179	
180	/-! ## The converse check: the reduction is not a weakening -/
181	
182	/-- **`IsChartUniv` forces elementwise injectivity of the restricted chart.**
183	
184	The converse direction of the reduction, and the reason it is a reduction rather than a
185	restatement: a lane that obtains `IsChartUniv` has, for free, the injectivity statement that
186	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` is the hard half of.  So there is no route to `hf` that
187	avoids relative GAP-2 — the gate is real, and this file has moved it rather than removed it.
188	
189	Compare `isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective`: that says the criterion cannot
190	be *satisfied* without injectivity; this says the goal cannot be *reached* without it. -/
191	theorem injective_of_isChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
192	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
193	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
194	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
195	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
196	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
197	    Function.Injective ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
198	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf h T
199	
200	end
201	
202	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap

/-!
# The unit of the étale sheafification: `relPicFunctor ⟶ picEtFunctor`

The Layer-2 étale Picard functor `picEt` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEt`,
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`) receives the honest relative Picard functor
through a natural transformation — the **unit of the étale sheafification**
(gap G4 of `informal/zeta-c2-rigidification-recon.md`, shared prerequisite of the
global (C2) comparison and of the degree/`Pic⁰` interface):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.fromSpecAffine T U`: the spectrum of the section ring of an
  affine open `U` of a test object `T`, as a test object over `T` — the bridge between
  the affine-opens indexing of `picEt` and the test-object indexing of `relPic`.  Its
  coherences: restriction (`fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom`) and naturality along an
  arbitrary test morphism (`fromSpecAffine_naturality`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt C T`: the component at `T` — a relative Picard class
  restricts along `fromSpecAffine T U` to every affine open, and each restriction is
  sent into the plus construction by `PicEtAff.unit`; the family is compatible by
  `PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit` and the coherences.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`: **affine consistency** — on an
  affine test the component collapses through the affine comparison
  (`picEtAffineEquiv`) to the unit `PicEtAff.unit` of the plus construction, so the
  Layer-2 unit extends the affine unit.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtUnit C : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`: the natural
  transformation (naturality through the `∃!`-API `picEt.IsPullbackValue` of
  `picEtMapVal`).

The (C2) comparison (`PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`, recon §1.3) will upgrade
the affine components to isomorphisms over section-admitting tests; injectivity of the
affine components is the landed (C1) `PicEtAff.unit_injective`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The affine-open test objects of a test object -/

namespace Over

/-- The spectrum of the section ring of an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, as a test object
over `T`: the underlying morphism is `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec`, and it lies over `Spec k`
by the very definition of the section-ring algebra `Over.sectionsAlgebra`. -/
def fromSpecAffine (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
    overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1) ⟶ T :=
  Over.homMk U.2.fromSpec (by
    have h1 : Spec.map (T.hom.appLE ⊤ U.1
          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge))
          ≫ (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (.of k))).fromSpec
        = U.2.fromSpec ≫ T.hom :=
      IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec T.hom (isAffineOpen_top _) U.2 _
    have h2 : (isAffineOpen_top (Spec (.of k))).fromSpec
        = Spec.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv := by
      rw [IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top, Scheme.isoSpec_Spec_inv]
    change U.2.fromSpec ≫ T.hom
        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(T.left, U.1)))
    rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Spec.map_comp, ← h2, h1])

/-- **Naturality of `fromSpecAffine`** along an arbitrary morphism of test objects:
for affine opens `W ≤ f⁻¹ V`, the section-ring pullback `Over.appLEAlgHom` intertwines
the affine-open test objects — `IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec` in the over
category. -/
theorem fromSpecAffine_naturality {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (V : T.left.affineOpens) (W : T'.left.affineOpens) (e : W.1 ≤ f.left ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) :

### §3.3 The `hf` certificate at `pic0SigmaSheaf` — the CHART-U interface (the DDR9-U pattern)

Target, frozen by §0.2.1: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f_c)` for every `c`; then
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161-171`) + DAT-B's joint
surjectivity finish Stage C.  For a test `T` with Σ-point `(a, λ)`,
`λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, the fibre product of `f_c` against `λ` is the
subfunctor of maps `T' → T` along which `λ` becomes a chart value.  Split, and pin
the boundary as a NAMED interface so the DAT-B lane slots in:

* **CHART-U(a) — the membership locus.**
  `chartLocus c λ := { t : T | the fibre class λ_t·θ^m·(−Σ) at κ(t) has an effective
  degree-g witness with h¹ = 0 }` — the field-point predicate, well-defined for plus
  classes through the DAT-4 collapse (`picEtAffineEquiv` naturality,
  `Picard/PicEtMap.lean`; degree part landed as `degAt`, `Pic0Functor.lean:54`; the
  h¹ part is the witness clause at the κ(t)-collapse — for classes reached through
  §3.2's `chartValue` this is (V1a) on the nose).  DAT-C states everything against
  `chartLocus`; membership-vs-fibre-product is the mono (§3.2) + normalization (§2).
  **STATUS 2026-07-28 (run 0072): `chartLocus` IS NOW DEFINED**, in
  `Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean`, in the (a-amendment) split form, over a general test, at
  the twisted class — sorry-free.  Three corrections this pass, all measured against the
  tree rather than inferred:

  * **The input list above was incomplete: there is a FOURTH input, prior to all three.**
    The predicate is a condition on *points of a general test*, and nothing in the tree
    converted a point of `T.left` into anything at which a class can be evaluated: every
    witness predicate is indexed by `q : PrimeSpectrum B` over an *affine* base, and every
    class is evaluated at a field point only through a morphism `overSpec k K ⟶ T` for an
    abstract `K`.  That conversion is `Over.testPoint` (`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`),
    built from mathlib's canonical `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, which makes
    chart-independence *free* rather than a well-definedness side condition.  (The affine
    -chart route — pick `U ∋ t`, use `IsAffineOpen.primeIdealOf` and
    `Over.fromSpecAffine` — was tried and abandoned: it needs an independence-of-`U`
    lemma before it can define anything.)
  * **The split predicate is `IsSplitWitness`**, and the amendment's "some (equivalently
    every)" is *not* symmetric in cost.  The ∃-form is the definition; the comparison of
    two splittings goes through a common separable extension
    (`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`, which rests on the co-owned
    `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`), not through a direct comparison.  The
    splitting itself is `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`
    (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`, landed) applied to the étale cover of the plus class.

    **The splitting is now its own theorem** (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`, `9f5d2a3e6`,
    sorry-free): `exists_splitting_of_picEt` — *every* plus class over a field is `relPicMk`
    of an honest Čech class over some finite separable extension, unconditionally and with no
    witness clause; and `isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` says `IsSplitWitness`
    is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  This matters for lane order rather than
    tidiness: `IsSplitWitness` is a twelve-component existential whose **first eight
    components exist for every class with no hypothesis**, and §1.2 of `w4-datb` needs the
    splitting fixed at step 1 so that `m` can be chosen at *that* field in step 3 (where the
    uniform bound provably does not exist) and the witness produced only at step 5.  As one
    existential the `m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled.

    Two elaboration hazards are recorded in that file and should not be re-discovered: the
    derived `Algebra k L` must be `clear_value`d before closing the existential (otherwise a
    composite instance term is substituted and the `overSpec k L` carriers are re-checked
    against it — no convergence in 1600000 heartbeats), and **no positional introduction rule
    exists**, deliberately: `IsSplitWitness` spells the base-changed curve two ways, so
    handing its tuple to one anonymous constructor while `L` is a metavariable does not
    elaborate at any budget tried.  Use `Iff.rfl` plus `.mpr` at a site where `L` is fixed.
  * **The twist has a class-side avatar now**: `chartTwist`.  ~~with `degAt_chartTwist` giving
    fibre degree `deg Z − m·d₁`, matching `degAt_chartValue` at `n = 0`~~ — **that was a SIGN
    ERROR and it made the locus VACUOUS.  Fixed 2026-07-28, `8ef9493ff`, issue I-0514.**

    `chartTwist` must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist.  `chartValue` is
    `abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`, so recovering the Abel class means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing
    by `Σ`: `chartTwist := λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, with `degAt_chartTwist = m·d₁ − deg Z = +g` under the
    chart-index constraint.  The earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving
    `−g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, **that locus was empty for every
    `g ≥ 1`** and CHART-U(b)'s openness of it was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
    `degAt_chartValue` at **`n = g`** (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands
    in `pic0`), not at `n = 0`.

    **Why no ledger caught it, and this is the transferable part:** the wrong-signed
    `degAt_chartTwist` was *internally consistent*.  It computed `−g` faithfully and its docstring
    said so out loud.  A degree ledger recomputes a sign error rather than detecting it.  The fix
    therefore ships an **inversion law** instead of just a corrected ledger:
    `chartTwist_chartValue : chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s`
    (by `group`), which is FALSE of the old definition.  Pin a direction with a round-trip law,
    not with a degree.

* **CHART-U(b) — openness of `chartLocus` (SHARED brick, DAT-B co-owner; honest new
  work, M→L).**

  **STATUS 2026-07-28 (run 0072): assembled CONDITIONALLY** in

  except one, and the file's header table names each with its anchor.  The residue is

  **TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW, both later on 2026-07-28 (run 0072), both retracting

  1. **The file is now sorry-free** (`e6a7b0582`).  The `sorry` at

     "transcription", and the three goals recorded at it were correct — but it was stated
     with the `Algebra A` / `IsScalarTower k A` structures on `κ(t)` as explicit `alg`/`tow`
     ARGUMENTS, and in that form **the statement is unprovable**: an arbitrary regrading of

  2. **"Producing it needs the mul/tensor half of GAP-1" is FALSE** (`a5da2f1a1`; see the
     retraction in §0.3).  The twist is ONE `thetaFamily` (`chartTwist_collapse`), so there
     is no datum product in the route; and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` presents any class
     including a product outright.  The residue of this row is therefore *only* the pointwise
     identification `IsChartDatumPresentation` — a `cechPicClass` base-change statement — and
     not any construction.

  **THIRD CORRECTION, 2026-07-29 (run 0072 r6, lane `ajcr-charts`): the residue's WITNESS half
  is discharged, so the row is now entirely a plus-class statement.**
  `IsChartDatumPresentation` is an `↔`; `Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationHalf.lean` proved the
  forward half by the trivial splitting and named the converse `hconv` (the descent direction:
  from a split witness at *some* `L_t/κ(t)`, produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)`).  `hconv`
  is now proved — `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at`,
  `Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`.

  **The transferable content is which ingredient was missing.**  That file's docstring priced
  the obstruction correctly ("the witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than
  visibly in `D`'s at `κ(t)`") and named two transport lemmas as the ingredients.  The step that
  makes the class *visible* is not a transport: it is `PicEtAff.unit_injective`
  (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1) — the unconditional close of the ζ3
  campaign) together with `relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton`, which force the presenting class
  to **equal** `D`'s fibre class at `L_t`.  Both have been in the tree for weeks and **no
  CHART-U row cites either**.

  So both halves of this row's residue are now witness-free, `H¹`-free and divisor-free, and
  what remains is exactly the `cechPicClass` base-change identity that correction 2 above
  predicted — at every extension of `κ(t)` rather than only at `κ(t)`, which is the one place
  the reduction is not tight (`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measures the gap: at `L := κ(t)`
  the two coincide by `Iff.rfl`).

  **FOURTH CORRECTION, 2026-07-29 (run 0072 r7, lane `ajcr-charts`): "at every extension rather
  than only at `κ(t)`" OVERPRICED THE GAP, and the reason it went unpriced is that the transport
  closing it was cited by name and never written.**

  `Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`'s header said it does "not silently assume the
  transport" because `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` was "the honest statement" of when
  the `κ(t)`-level `hfib` gives the `L`-level one.  **That declaration existed nowhere in the
  tree.**  The effect was worse than a dangling reference: the sentence made the `hplus` side
  condition read as bookkeeping already discharged, while `hplus` was the *whole* of this row's
  remaining content — and a `sorry` census, an axiom probe and a green root build are all silent
  about a docstring naming a declaration that does not exist.

  **The gap is zero.**  `hplus` at `L` is `hfib` at `κ(t)` pushed forward along
  `PicEtAff.map C L`: `PicEtAff.map_map` on the left, `PicEtAff.map_unit` on the right, and
  `relCurveMap_comp` over `k → A → κ(t) → L` to identify the two-step pull of `D.cechPicClass`
  with the one-step pull.  Three functoriality laws, no geometry, and nothing specific to
  `cechPicClass` at all.  All three had been in the tree for weeks.  So
  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measured the gap from below and the transport now measures it
  from above, and the generalisation in `L` costs nothing.

  **Use `isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower`** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean`):
  `IsChartDatumPresentation` from `hfib` **alone**.

  **A second r7 finding, about a statement rather than a proof, and it is the more transferable
  one.**  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at`'s `hplus` binder quantifies
  `(_ : Algebra A L)` universally with only `IsScalarTower k A L`.  That is strictly stronger than
  its own proof consumes — the proof takes the `A`-structure from its `htow` argument and uses
  `hplus` at *that* instance only — and the extra strength is not harmless:
  `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, so at an `Algebra A L` unrelated to the
  composite `A → κ(t) → L` the right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a *different*
  morphism and `hfib` cannot imply it.  So the `∀`-form is not merely hard to supply — it is the
  wrong statement.  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower` adds
  `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` to that binder: exactly the third component
  `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns, and which the landed proof already destructures
  and then discards.  A hypothesis can be over-strong *inside a binder*, and a census sees
  argument positions, not the instances they quantify.

  **THE ROW'S ENDPOINT, and what it still does not claim.**
  `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`) is CHART-U(b) at a
  general test from a witness-free hypothesis: per affine piece of the test, one

  identification of the datum's fibre class with `μ`'s fibre, which for the Σ-chart's `μ` is where
  §1.2's twist bookkeeping enters.  That is a different obligation from every link in the chain
  above, and it is now the whole of what CHART-U(b) owes.

  **A correction to r7's own evidence, because the instrument matters more than the claim.**  The

  The datum-worksheet §2.3 chain, now fully landed except its last

10	# Field points of a general test from points of its space — CHART-U(a) input 0
11	
12	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 freezes `chartLocus c λ` as a **subset of a general
13	test** `T`: a set of *points* `t : T.left`, at each of which one reads the fibre class of
14	`λ` at the residue field `κ(t)`.  `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it and
15	lists three missing inputs (the shifted-datum constructor, the split predicate, the
16	descent/étale-image transports).
17	
18	**There is a fourth, prior to all three, and it is why nothing in the tree implements
19	`chartLocus`.**  The two vocabularies the definition has to join do not meet anywhere:
20	
21	* every witness/vanishing predicate in the tree is indexed by a prime of an **affine**
22	  base — `q : PrimeSpectrum B`, fibre field `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`
23	  (`Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:80`, `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean:82`,
24	  `DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:363`);
25	* every *class* is evaluated at a field point only through a **morphism**
26	  `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` for an abstract field `K` (`degAt`, `Pic0Functor.lean:54`;
27	  `pic0Subgroup`, `:107`).
28	
29	Nothing converts a point of `T.left` into either.  This file is that conversion, and it
30	is deliberately kept free of the chart layer: no `chartLocus`, no `θ`, no `Σ`, no
31	`divRep`.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField t` — the residue field `κ(t)` of a point of
36	  `T.left`, as a `k`-algebra (`Scheme.residueField`, with the `k`-algebra structure
37	  pulled back along the structure morphism).
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint t` — **the bridge**: the field point
39	  `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` supported at `t`.  Built from mathlib's
40	  `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, whose triangle over `Spec k` is the `Over` datum.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_base` — it really is supported at `t`: the unique
42	  point of `Spec κ(t)` maps to `t`.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_comp` — **naturality**, the law every well-definedness
44	  argument downstream runs on: for `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, the field point of `t`
45	  followed by `f` is the field point of `f t`, up to the residue-field extension
46	  `κ(f t) → κ(t)` that `f` induces.  Stated as a commuting square rather than an equality
47	  of morphisms out of one object, because the two sides have different sources.

53	
54	The obvious route (pick an affine open `U ∋ t`, use `q := U.2.primeIdealOf t` and

129	      = (Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)).hom :=

144	  have hcomp : ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ (overSpec k A).hom)
145	      = (overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t

147	  -- `Spec.preimage` is injective on the composite, and the composite identity is `hcomp`.

151	      = (algebraMap A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).comp
152	          (algebraMap k A) := by

154	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
155	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)
156	            ≫ Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)) := by
157	      rw [Spec.map_comp, Spec.map_preimage]
158	      rfl
159	    rw [this, Spec.preimage_map]
160	    rfl
161	  exact hw.trans hsplit
162	
163	end Affine

166	
167	/-- **The bridge: a point of `T.left` as a field point of `T`.**
168	
169	`t : T.left` names the test object morphism `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` whose carrier is
170	mathlib's canonical `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` and whose triangle over `Spec k` holds
171	by the very definition of the `k`-algebra structure on `κ(t)`.
172	
173	This is the missing input 0 of CHART-U(a): with it, `{t : T.left | P (fibre of λ at
174	κ(t))}` is a legal `Set T.left` for any predicate `P` on classes over a field, and that

176	def testPoint {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :

178	  Over.homMk (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t)
179	    (Spec.map_preimage (T.left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ T.hom)).symm
180	
181	@[simp]
182	lemma testPoint_left {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left) :
183	    (testPoint t).left = T.left.fromSpecResidueField t :=
184	  rfl

186	/-- **The field point is supported at the point it came from**: the unique point of
187	`Spec κ(t)` maps to `t`.  (`Spec` of a field has a unique point, so this pins the support
188	completely.) -/
189	@[simp]
190	lemma testPoint_base {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (t : T.left)
191	    (s : (overSpec k (testPointField t)).left) :
192	    (testPoint t).left.base s = t :=
193	  Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply t s
194	
195	/-! ## Naturality along a morphism of tests
196	
197	The law every downstream well-definedness argument runs on.  A morphism `f : T' ⟶ T`
198	does not send the field point of `t` to the field point of `f t` on the nose — the two
199	have *different sources*, `Spec κ(t)` and `Spec κ(f t)`.  What is true, and what the
200	transports of `w4-datb` §1.6 use, is that the square through the induced residue-field
201	extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` commutes. -/
202	
203	/-- **The residue-field extension a morphism of tests induces at a point**, as a
204	`k`-algebra map `κ(f t) → κ(t)`.  This is `Scheme.Hom.residueFieldMap` with its
205	`k`-algebra structure read off; it is the extension along which every fibre-field
206	predicate has to be invariant for a locus over `T` to pull back to one over `T'`. -/

208	    CommRingCat.of (testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t))
209	      ⟶ CommRingCat.of (testPointField (T := T') t) :=
210	  f.left.residueFieldMap t
211	
212	/-- The residue-field extension of `testPointFieldMap`, as an algebra structure: `κ(t)` is

16	carrier locus: for a prime `q` of the carrier over `p`, the residue-field extension
17	`κ(q)/κ(p)` is separable (étale/étale-plus carrier) and must **preserve** the witness
18	h¹-vanishing of the fibre class.
19	
20	That content is `chartLocus`-free (I-0252's phrasing through the still-undefined
21	`chartLocus`, DAT-C C9, is pure plumbing on top) and is landed here in the **witness
22	form** `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
23	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`) uses.  The heart is a single module fact:
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff` — for an `S`-module `H`
26	  and a field extension `L → L'` in the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is subsingleton iff
27	  `H ⊗[S] L'` is.  Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the
28	  (nonzero) field extension.  **Separability is not needed** — every field extension is
29	  faithfully flat; it is the geometric packaging (étale carrier) that makes the residue
30	  extensions separable, not the transfer.
31	
32	Read through the two-way datum dictionary
33	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6) — under
34	which the witness predicate at a field `L` is exactly the engine's complex-form fibre
35	condition `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)` — this gives:
36	
37	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing` — the field-parametrised witness
38	  predicate; for `L = κ(q)` it is membership of `q` in the keystone-1 locus.
39	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` — **the gap-2
40	  core**: witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'` for any field
41	  extension `L → L'` in the `k`/`B` tower.
42	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable` — the separable
43	  specialisation the CHART-U(b) consumer names (`Algebra.IsSeparable`).
44	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq` — the fixed-
45	  field class-intrinsicity (V1a): the witness predicate depends only on the mapped fibre
46	  class, so two data with equal fibre class at `L` have the same predicate.
47	
48	## What the CHART-U(b) / C9 assembly consumes and the residual (I-0252 gap 2)
49	
50	The `comap`-preimage identity keystone 3 needs, `comap f ⁻¹'(chartLocus_A) = locus_B`,
51	reduces pointwise (for `q` over `p`, `κ(q)/κ(p)` separable) to two links:
52	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` field transfer, landed
53	here) composed with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq` at the fixed field
54	`κ(q)` (landed here).  The **residual** is the input to the latter — the shifted-datum
55	class identity `map (relCurveMap … κ(q)) D_A.cechPicClass = map (relCurveMap … κ(q))
56	D_B.cechPicClass` (I-0252 gap 1, the Σ/θ naturality) — and the `chartLocus` definition
57	itself (DAT-C C9).  Both are divRep/C9-gated; neither is a mathematical wall on the
58	invariance itself, which is complete.

81	/-! ## The module-theoretic core -/
82	
83	/-- **Base change of a module along a field extension preserves triviality**: for an
84	`S`-module `H` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the `S`-tower, `H ⊗[S] L` is
85	subsingleton iff `H ⊗[S] L'` is.
86	
87	Going up is `0 ⊗ = 0`; coming down is the faithful flatness of the (nonzero) field
88	extension `L → L'` (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality`), read across the
89	base-change-in-stages equivalence `(TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange)`.
90	**Separability is not used** — every field extension is faithfully flat. -/
91	theorem subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
92	    {S L L' H : Type u} [CommRing S] [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra S L] [Algebra S L']
93	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower S L L'] [AddCommGroup H] [Module S H] :
94	    Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L) ↔ Subsingleton (H ⊗[S] L') := by
95	  have e := TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange S L L' L' H
96	  rw [(TensorProduct.comm S H L).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
97	      (TensorProduct.comm S H L').toEquiv.subsingleton_congr,
98	      ← e.toEquiv.subsingleton_congr]
99	  exact ⟨fun _ => inferInstance,
100	    fun _ => Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_reflects_triviality L L' (L ⊗[S] H)⟩
101	
102	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
103	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
104	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
105	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
106	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

108	/-! ## The witness predicate as a function of the fibre field -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart-membership witness predicate at a field `L`** — the field-parametrised
111	form of the set of `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`
112	(`Pic0ChartLocusOpen`): the fibre class of `D` at `L` admits an effective witness divisor
113	with vanishing `H¹`.  For `L = q.asIdeal.ResidueField` this is definitionally membership
114	of `q` in the keystone-1 witness locus. -/
115	def BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
116	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [IsScalarTower k B L] : Prop :=
117	  ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
118	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
119	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
120	      ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
121	
122	/-- The witness predicate is the engine's complex-form fibre condition
123	`Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L)`, via the two-way datum dictionary
124	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6). -/
125	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton
126	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
127	    [IsScalarTower k B L] :
128	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] L) :=
129	  (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness L).symm
130	
131	/-! ## The fibre-field invariance (the gap-2 core) -/
132	
133	/-- **CHART-U(b) gap-2 core — fibre-field invariance of witness h¹-vanishing**: for a
134	pinned datum `D` over the affine base `B` and a field extension `L → L'` inside the
135	`k`/`B` tower (the residue-field seam `κ(p) → κ(q)` of a carrier map `comap f`), the
136	witness h¹-vanishing of `D` at `L` transfers to and from `L'`.
137	
138	Both sides are, via the datum dictionary, `Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] ·)`, and
139	that transfers along the (faithfully flat) field extension `L → L'`
140	(`subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff`).  In particular this covers the separable
141	residue-field extensions of an étale/étale-plus carrier map. -/
142	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
143	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
144	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
145	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
146	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] :
147	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' := by
148	  rw [D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L,
149	      D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton L']
150	  exact subsingleton_tensorProduct_field_ext_iff
151	
152	/-- **The separable specialisation the CHART-U(b) transport (ii) names** (I-0252 gap 2):
153	for a **separable** residue-field extension `L → L'` (`Algebra.IsSeparable`, the case of
154	an étale/étale-plus carrier map), witness h¹-vanishing of `D` transfers between `L` and
155	`L'`.  Separability is recorded to name the intended consumer; the transfer holds for any
156	field extension (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`). -/
157	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable
158	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
159	    (L L' : Type u) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra k L] [Algebra k L']
160	    [Algebra B L] [Algebra B L'] [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B L']
161	    [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower B L L'] [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] :
162	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L' :=
163	  D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension L L'
164	
165	/-! ## Fixed-field class-intrinsicity (the other half the `comap` identity needs) -/
166	
167	/-- **Class-intrinsicity of the witness predicate at a fixed field** (V1a): the witness
168	h¹-vanishing predicate depends only on the mapped fibre class
169	`Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass`, so two data — over possibly
170	different bases `B`, `B'` — whose fibre classes at `L` agree have the same witness
171	predicate at `L`.
172	
173	Together with `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` (the `κ(p) → κ(q)` transfer)
174	this is exactly what the CHART-U(b) `comap`-preimage identity reduces to at C9-time; the
175	one residual input is the shifted-datum class identity of I-0252 gap 1 (the Σ/θ
176	naturality), which is divRep-gated. -/
177	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq
178	    {B' : Type u} [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B']
179	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (D' : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B' π)
180	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra B' L]
181	    [IsScalarTower k B L] [IsScalarTower k B' L]
182	    (hcl : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass
183	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B' L) D'.cechPicClass) :
184	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L ↔ D'.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
185	  simp only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hcl]

11	/-!
12	# CHART-U(b)'s last residue: the descent direction `hconv`
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationHalf.lean` splits `IsChartDatumPresentation` into a forward half
15	(proved there, by the trivial splitting) and a converse `hconv`, and its docstring prices the
16	converse as follows:
17	
18	> `hconv` is the descent direction: from a split witness over *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)`
19	> chosen per point, produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself.  Its two ingredients both
20	> exist — `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries a *datum* predicate across a
21	> field extension, and `hfib` identifies the classes — but composing them is not a rewrite,
22	> because the witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s at
23	> `κ(t)`.
24	
25	**That diagnosis is right, and it names two of the three ingredients.**  The missing one is
26	the reason the composition is not a rewrite: to see the received witness as lying in `D`'s
27	fibre class one must go *backwards* through `PicEtAff.unit`, and that step is
28	`PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`) — the unconditional close of the
29	ζ3 campaign, Kleiman 2.5(1).  With it the descent is three steps and no geometry:
30	
31	1. the split witness at `L_t` gives a presenting class `M` with
32	   `PicEtAff.map … (picEtAffineEquiv … μ_t) = PicEtAff.unit … (relPicMk … M)` and a witness
33	   divisor in `M` with vanishing `H¹`;
34	2. `hfib` at `t`, transported to `L_t`, says the *same* left-hand side equals
35	   `PicEtAff.unit … (relPicMk … (D's fibre class at L_t))`.  `unit_injective` then makes the
36	   two `relPicMk` arguments equal, and `relPicMk` is injective too — so `M` **is** `D`'s fibre
37	   class at `L_t`, which is what "visibly in `D`'s class" was missing;
38	3. hence `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L_t` holds by definition, and
39	   `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` brings it down to `κ(t)`.
40	
41	## What this file does and does not close
42	
43	It closes `hconv` **from a per-point transported `hfib`** — the statement
44	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` below, which is `hfib`'s identity read at the chosen extension
45	rather than at `κ(t)`.  That is a real reduction: `hconv`'s conclusion is a statement about
46	witnesses and `H¹`, and what remains is a statement about *plus classes only*, with no witness,
47	no `H¹` and no divisor — exactly the shape §0.3's GAP-6 dictionary cannot see and the shape
48	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre` already has at `κ(t)`.
49	
50	**CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (r7), and this paragraph is why it is worth reading.**  The sentence that
51	stood here said the transport was not silently assumed because
52	`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` was "the honest statement" of it — and **that
53	declaration did not exist**, in this file or anywhere in the tree.  It was advertised by name and
54	never written (the failure mode `docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`), and the effect was worse
55	than a dangling reference: the sentence made `hplus` read as bookkeeping already discharged, while
56	`hplus` was in fact the *whole* of B-4's remaining content.  The last clause — "so the composite
57	needs `hfib` at `κ(t)` and nothing else" — was therefore false of the theorem actually below it,
58	which takes `hplus` as a hypothesis.
59	
60	**It is true now, and of a different theorem.**  `Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean` proves the
61	transport (three functoriality laws — `PicEtAff.map_map`, `PicEtAff.map_unit`, `relCurveMap_comp`
62	— and no geometry) and derives `IsChartDatumPresentation` from `hfib` alone as
63	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower`.  **Prefer that theorem**; the one below remains
64	correct and is the general form.
65	
66	**One further finding, about the statement of `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` below
67	rather than its proof.**  Its `hplus` binder quantifies `(_ : Algebra A L)` universally with only
68	the `k`-tower imposed, and that is strictly stronger than the proof consumes: the proof takes the
69	`A`-structure from its own `htow` and uses `hplus` at *that* instance only.  The extra strength is
70	not harmless — `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, so at an `Algebra A L`
71	unrelated to the composite `A → κ(t) → L` the right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a
72	different morphism and `hfib` cannot imply it.  So the `∀`-form is not merely hard to supply, it
73	is the wrong statement.  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower` (same file as the
74	transport) is this theorem with `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` added to that binder — the third
75	component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns, and which the proof below already
76	destructures and then discards.
77	
78	## Main declarations
79	
80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` — the plus-class identity at a *given*
81	  extension of the residue field.  Witness-free.
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` — **the descent step**: a
83	  split witness whose splitting field satisfies that identity gives the datum's predicate
84	  there, hence (by the field-extension `iff`) at `κ(t)`.  This is where
85	  `PicEtAff.unit_injective` is spent.
86	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` — **CHART-U(b)'s residue closed
87	  modulo the plus-class identity**: `IsChartDatumPresentation` from `hfib` at `κ(t)` together
88	  with the per-point transported identity, with no separate `hconv`.
89	-/

117	variable (C π) in
118	/-- **The plus-class identity of `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, read at a given extension `L` of the
119	residue field** rather than at `κ(t)` itself.
120	
121	Witness-free, `H¹`-free and divisor-free, exactly like `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`: it says the
122	plus class obtained by restricting `μ` to `κ(t)` and then reading it over `L` is the plus-unit
123	of `D`'s fibre class at `L`.
124	
125	This is the form the descent step below consumes, because a split witness for `μ` at `t`
126	produces its data over an extension it chooses, not over `κ(t)`. -/
127	def IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
128	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
129	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
130	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
131	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] [Algebra A L]
132	    [IsScalarTower k A L] : Prop :=
133	  PicEtAff.map C L
134	      (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
135	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ))
136	    = PicEtAff.unit C L
137	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
138	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass))

140	/-! ## The descent step -/
141	
142	variable (C π) in
143	/-- **THE DESCENT STEP** — `hconv` at one point, given the plus-class identity at the
144	splitting field.
145	
146	A split witness for `μ`'s fibre at `t` hands over a finite separable `L/κ(t)`, a presenting
147	class `M` over `L`, and a divisor `W` in `M` with vanishing `H¹`.  The plus-class identity at
148	`L` says the *same* left-hand side that `M` presents is the plus-unit of `D`'s fibre class at
149	`L`.  So:
150	
151	* `PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1) — the
152	  unconditional close of the ζ3 campaign) makes the two `relPicMk` arguments equal;
153	* `relPicMk` is injective (`relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton`), so `M` **is** `D`'s fibre
154	  class at `L`;
155	* `W` therefore witnesses `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L` by definition, and
156	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries that down to `κ(t)`.
157	
158	**This is the ingredient `Pic0ChartPresentationHalf`'s docstring was missing.**  It diagnosed
159	correctly that "the witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s
160	at `κ(t)`", and named the two transport lemmas — but the step that makes the class *visible*
161	is not a transport at all: it is the injectivity of the plus unit, which the tree has had since
162	the ζ3 close and which no CHART-U row cites. -/
163	theorem hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
164	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
165	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)
166	    (hplus : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
167	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
168	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
169	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
170	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
171	    (htow : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
172	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      Σ' (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
175	        IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
176	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
177	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
178	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
179	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := htow L hLf hLk hLK hLtow
180	  -- the plus-class identity at `L`, and the presenting identity the witness came with
181	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
182	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
183	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
184	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
185	    rw [← hM]
186	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow
187	  -- `unit_injective` then `relPicMk` injective: `M` IS `D`'s fibre class at `L`
188	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
189	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
190	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
191	  -- so `W` witnesses `D`'s predicate at `L`, and the field-extension `iff` descends it
192	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
193	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
194	  rw [hW, hMcl]

196	/-! ## The `htow` hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed
197	
198	`htow` returns *data* (three instances), so it could in principle be an unmeetable demand and
199	the descent step vacuous — the failure mode memory `isolating-a-residue-as-a-class` records
200	from the other direction.  It is not: the composite tower always exists. -/
201	
202	/-- **`htow` is constructible**, at any `L` over the residue field.
203	
204	The `A`-algebra structure on `L` is the composite `A → κ(t) → L`, where `A → κ(t)` is the
205	tree's own `Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`.  Both towers then hold by
206	`IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq`.
207	
208	Worth stating rather than inlining, because `Algebra A L` does **not** synthesize from the
209	hypotheses of `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` — measured — so a reader would
210	otherwise have to guess whether `htow` is a genuine obligation or bookkeeping.  It is
211	bookkeeping, and this is the proof. -/
212	def towerOfResidueFieldExtension {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
213	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
214	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
215	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] :
216	    Σ' (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
217	      IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L := by
218	  letI : Algebra A L :=
219	    ((algebraMap (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).comp
220	      (algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t))).toAlgebra
221	  haveI htow : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L :=
222	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
223	  refine ⟨_, IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x => ?_, htow⟩
224	  change (algebraMap k L) x
225	      = (algebraMap (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
226	          ((algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) ((algebraMap k A) x))
227	  rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t),
228	    ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
229	
230	/-- **`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` at `L := κ(t)` IS `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` at `t`** — by
231	`Iff.rfl`, so the generalisation in `L` is a genuine generalisation of the *same* equation and
232	not a different statement that happens to specialise.
233	
234	This is the upper half of the two-sided check on `hplus` below, and it is the sharp one: it shows
235	the extra strength of `hplus` over `hfib` is exactly "the same identity at every extension", so a
236	lane reading `hplus` knows precisely what it owes beyond `hfib` — the naturality of `cechPicClass`
237	along `κ(t) → L`, and nothing else.
238	
239	**The lower half was measured too, and is recorded here because it cannot be a theorem.**  A
240	reduction whose new hypothesis is *satisfiable by construction* is vacuous, and `D` in
241	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` is chosen by the consumer — exactly the configuration in which that
242	happens.  Probed at arbitrary `μ`, `D`, `t`, `L`: `rfl` fails on the left-hand side, and `simp`
243	and `aesop` both leave unsolved goals.  So it is a genuine equation between two plus classes and
244	not a `Prop` true for free.  (A passing automation attempt would have refuted the reduction, which
245	is why the probe is worth running before pricing anything as a residue.)
246	
247	**And the probe has a second form, which the first does not cover.**  Junk-inhabitation is the risk
248	when the hypothesis is *consumer-chosen* — `D` here.  When it is *determined* by the setting, the
249	mirror risk is **unsatisfiability**: a reduction to a false hypothesis passes every `sorry` census
250	and every axiom probe, because it then *is* a theorem.  `hplus` is determined in `μ`, so that
251	direction needs a witness, and the witness is landed and unconditional:
252	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` produces, for **any** plus class over **any** reading field, a finite
253	separable `L` and a presenting class `M` with exactly the identity `hplus` asserts.  So the
254	plus-class identity is *inhabited* at every `μ`, not merely consistent. -/
255	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
256	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
257	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (h : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
258	    IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
259	  h t
260	
261	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue, assembled -/
262	
263	variable (C π) in
264	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` WITH NO SEPARATE `hconv`** — CHART-U(b)'s residue reduced to a
265	witness-free statement about plus classes.
266	
267	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse` asks for `hfib` *and* `hconv`.  This asks
268	for `hfib` and the per-point plus-class identity at the splitting field, which is `hfib`'s own
269	statement read at `L` instead of at `κ(t)` — and discharges `hconv` from it via the descent step
270	above.  `htow` is supplied by `towerOfResidueFieldExtension`, so it is not an
271	obligation on the caller.
272	
273	**What this buys the CHART-U(b) row.**  Its residue was "the pointwise presentation", an `↔`
274	one half of which involved witnesses and `H¹`.  Both halves are now witness-free: the forward
275	one was already (`isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing`, by the trivial splitting) and the
276	converse is now, by the plus-unit injectivity.  So the whole of CHART-U(b) reduces to
277	`cechPicClass` base-change identities — which is what the row's own §0.3 retraction predicted
278	("a `cechPicClass` base-change statement, and not any construction") and what
279	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s header calls the residue.
280	
281	**What it does not buy — SUPERSEDED 2026-07-29 (r7).**  This paragraph said the remaining identity
282	is at *every* extension `L` of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` asks, and that
283	whether the two are equivalent "is the naturality of `cechPicClass` under `κ(t) → L`, which this
284	file does not settle".  **They are equivalent, and the answer was cheaper than the framing
285	suggested**: the identity at `L` is the identity at `κ(t)` pushed forward along `PicEtAff.map C L`,
286	so it needs `PicEtAff.map_map`, `PicEtAff.map_unit` and `relCurveMap_comp` and nothing about
287	`cechPicClass` specifically.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower`
288	(`Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean`) is the transport, and
289	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower` is this theorem with the `hplus` argument
290	removed.  Use that one.
291	
292	The one caveat the transport does carry is the tower compatibility `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L`, which
293	is genuinely needed (see the correction in this file's header) and is supplied by
294	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` — so it is not an obligation on any caller. -/
295	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
296	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
297	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D)
298	    (hplus : ∀ (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
299	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
300	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
301	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
302	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L) :
303	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D :=
304	  isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse C π hfib fun t =>
305	    hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at C π μ D t (hplus t)
306	      (fun L _ _ _ _ => towerOfResidueFieldExtension t L)
307	
308	end

9	/-!
10	# COV-1 input 1: the twisted class splits with a COMPUTABLE Čech representative
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean` says every plus class over a field is `relPicMk` of an honest
13	Čech class over *some* finite separable extension.  For the coverage theorem (`w4-datb` §1.2)
14	that is not enough by itself: the class under test is the *twisted* class
15	`λ_t · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and COV-1 must know what its presenting Čech class IS, because step 2
16	of the route computes the presenting class's DEGREE and steps 4–5 build a witness divisor
17	inside that class.  A bare `∃ M` gives the degree of nothing.
18	
19	## What this file adds
20	
21	`exists_splitting_chartTwist` splits the twisted class **and identifies the presenting
22	class** as
23	
24	  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`,
25	
26	where `M₀` presents the untwisted fibre class over the same `L`.  So the twist survives
27	the splitting *as an explicit factor*, and its degree is computable by the landed ledger:
28	`classDeg` of a base-changed class is base-field invariant (E-iv-alg,
29	`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`), so the twist contributes exactly
30	`m·d₁ − deg Z` and nothing else.
31	
32	Two landed facts make this cheap, and both were established by this lane earlier today:
33	
34	* `chartTwist_collapse` (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) — the twist is ONE
35	  `thetaFamily`, at the single base class `chartTwistClass C m Z`.  There is no product of
36	  families to split.
37	* `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv` (`Picard/ThetaShift.lean:122`) — a θ-family is
38	  **already honest at every affine test**: its affine collapse is the plus *unit* of the
39	  base-changed base class, with no cover and no extension.  So the twist factor needs no
40	  splitting at all; only the `λ`-factor does.
41	
42	That second point is the content.  A reader who expects "split a product of two plus
43	classes" would look for a common refinement of two étale covers.  There is none to find:
44	one factor is honest over every base, so the splitting of the product is the splitting of
45	the other factor.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48	
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk` — a θ-family is honest at
50	  every affine test: its collapse is the plus *unit* of the base-changed base class.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_base_comp` — the base comparison factors through any
52	  intermediate field of the tower.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit` — **the twisted class
54	  splits with its presenting class NAMED**: `M₀ · (twist class base-changed to L)`.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` — the positional introduction rule
56	  for `IsSplitWitness`, and the retraction below.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self` — its `L := K` case.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass` — what COV-1 consumes: a witness
59	  divisor for the named class certifies `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class.
60	
61	## A RETRACTION this file carries
62	
63	`isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` is a positional introduction rule for `IsSplitWitness`,
64	which this lane had recorded as **impossible** (the closing note of
65	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`, and memory item I-0564: "measured three times, do not retry").
66	The old measurement tested five ways of handing the twelve components to *one* anonymous
67	constructor, and all five do time out.  It did not test **staging** them: eight `Exists.intro`s
68	in sequence cost nothing at the default heartbeat budget, because `L` is fixed at the first
69	step and the two curve spellings never race as metavariables.  The trivial splitting `L := K`,
70	named in that record as the variant worth wanting, follows in one line.  See the theorem's
71	docstring for the diagnosis and the corrected rule.
72	-/

74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
76	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

92	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
93	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
94	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
95	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

99	/-! ## The θ-family is honest at every field point -/
100	
101	variable (C) in
102	/-- **A θ-family is honest at every affine test**, in the `PicEtAff` spelling the split
103	predicate uses: its affine collapse is the plus unit of `relPicMk` of the base-changed base
104	class.
105	
106	This is `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv` (`Picard/ThetaShift.lean:122`) plus
107	`relPicAlgMap_mk`, and it is the reason the twist needs no splitting: `PicEtAff.unit` is
108	already the honest reading, so no étale cover ever enters for this factor. -/
109	theorem picEtAffineEquiv_thetaFamily_eq_unit_relPicMk
110	    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
111	    picEtAffineEquiv C A (thetaFamily C L₀ (overSpec k A))
112	      = PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A)
113	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k A) L₀)) := by
114	  rw [thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv C L₀ A, relPicAlgMap_mk]
115	  rfl
116	
117	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
118	variable (C) in
119	/-- **The base-change comparison composes**: the relative-curve comparison down to the base
120	factors through any intermediate field of the tower.  Both sides are `C ◁ Spec` of a
121	`k`-algebra map into `L`, and there is only one such map out of `k`. -/
122	theorem relCurveMap_base_comp {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
123	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L] :
124	    relCurveMap C k L
125	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k K L)).left ≫ relCurveMap C k K := by
126	  rw [relCurveMap, relCurveMap, ← Over.comp_left, ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
127	  refine congrArg (fun ψ : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k k => (C ◁ ψ).left)
128	    (Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_)
129	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))
130	    = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))
131	      ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))
132	  rw [← Spec.map_comp]
133	  refine congrArg Spec.map (CommRingCat.hom_ext ?_)
134	  exact (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k K L).symm ▸ rfl
